status.en: No armed incidents reported in the past seven days; 0 in the past 30.
status.nb: Ingen væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene; 0 de siste 30.

summary.en: The incident monitor records no armed incidents in the past seven days or the past 30 days, and none were covered by multiple outlets. Nonetheless, recent reports describe a child killed and two injured while crossing into Lebanon, investigations of possible intrusions in northern Israel, arrests of suspected Hezbollah members transporting explosives, and drone or aerial strikes near the Lebanon‑Syria border. The UCDP notes 4,335 battle‑related deaths in 2024, reflecting the ongoing intensity of the Israel‑Hezbollah conflict.
summary.nb: Overvåkingen viser ingen væpnede hendelser de siste syv dagene eller de siste 30 dagene, og ingen ble dekket av flere medier. Likevel beskriver nylige rapporter et barn som ble drept og to såret ved grensekryssing til Libanon, etterforskning av mulig inntrengning i nordlige Israel, pågripelse av mistenkte Hezbollah‑medlemmer som fraktet sprengstoff, samt drone‑ eller luftangrep nær Libanon‑Syria‑grensen. UCDP registrerer 4 335 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, noe som gjenspeiler den pågående intensiteten i konflikten mellom Israel og Hezbollah.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
